extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, potential authors, and journal editors interested in arXiv-overlay and open-access publishing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and procedural standards for submitting and publishing mathematics papers via an arXiv-overlay journal (Discrete Analysis): posting to arXiv with a permissive license, submitting through Scholastica, peer review, author-managed typesetting, and publication metadata/links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diamond open access model
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrete Analysis will follow a 'diamond open access' model, meaning that it will be completely free for both authors and readers, with no subscription or article processing charge (APC) costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal sustains no-cost access by publishing solely via arXiv overlay rather than producing print issues or electronically hosting papers; goal is to lower cost barriers to making research open access.

rubrics_metrics.name: ArXiv overlay publishing (no hosting/typesetting by journal)
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal will publish solely via arXiv overlay, avoiding all overhead publishing costs including typesetting, which authors with a firm grasp of LaTeX can handle on their own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By replacing traditional paid publisher services (e.g., typesetting) with technology and author-managed preparation, the journal avoids hosting and production expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to post to arXiv using CC-BY-4.0
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors will submit to the journal by posting their papers to arXiv preprints using a CC-BY-4.0 license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posting to arXiv under CC-BY-4.0 is a prerequisite for completing submission to Discrete Analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission flow via Scholastica after arXiv posting
rubrics_metrics.description: Once articles have been posted on arXiv, in order to complete their submission to Discrete Analysis authors will visit the journal's Scholastica page, click 'submit,' and follow the series of simple submission steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholastica is used to manage the submission and peer review workflow; the arXiv posting plus the Scholastica 'submit' action constitute the submission procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review follows traditional journal workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrete Analysis will operate in much the same way as traditional journals, following the peer review process; the journal's editors will assess manuscripts and assign them to reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review is coordinated on Scholastica; editorial assessment and reviewer assignment mirror conventional editorial practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial coordination and use of Scholastica for review
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal’s editors will assess manuscripts and assign them to reviewers, coordinating peer review on Scholastica.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholastica handles reviewer assignment, correspondence, and peer review management for the editorial board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance and official publication metadata on arXiv
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted papers will be published on arXiv with all final edits and will be assigned an article number, DOI, and publication date in order to be officially added to Discrete Analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal's official record is implemented by marking the arXiv version as the peer-reviewed/final version and providing standard identifiers (article number, DOI, publication date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal website listings with brief descriptions and links
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal plans to publish brief descriptions of all of its published papers on its website accompanied by links to the articles on arXiv, giving readers the ability to easily browse the journal's content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Website entries serve as the journal's browsing interface while the full text remains on arXiv; descriptions are brief and link to the arXiv-hosted article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for author updates to arXiv articles and listing updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors will also have the ability to update their articles and request that the journal's editors include those updates in the article listing along with the link to the official peer-reviewed version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can make updates on arXiv post-publication and ask editors to reflect those updates in the journal's listing, enabling iterative improvements while keeping the arXiv record central.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical scope / fit for submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrete Analysis will be broad in scope, accepting papers on subjects that are broadly related to additive combinatorics, including: harmonic analysis, ergodic theory, topological dynamics, growth in groups, analytic number theory, combinatorial number theory, extremal combinatorics, probabilistic combinatorics, combinatorial geometry, convexity, metric geometry, and mathematically focused theoretical computer science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure their work is broadly related to additive combinatorics or the listed subfields to be within the journal's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial leadership and board as quality/oversight signal
rubrics_metrics.description: Gowers will serve as the managing editor along with a distinguished editorial board (named individuals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence of prominent editors (e.g., Gowers, Tao, others) signals editorial standards and oversight; submissions will be evaluated under their stewardship, though specific review criteria are those of peer review described above.
